title: The Line Up
paragraphs: A police procedural centered on criminal investigations, lineup interrogations, and the work of San Francisco detectives.
Realistic CBS police procedural set in an unnamed great American city. Bill Johnstone played Lt.

The run breaks into several distinct periods: Guthrie and Greb era (July 6, 1950 to December 27, 1951) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] and Guthrie and Karger era (1952-01 to February 20, 1953) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]].

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Eddie Dunstedter (music, composer, and conductor), William Johnstone (performer), Jaime del Valle (producer, director, and transcriber), [[person|howard-mcnear|Howard McNear]] (performer), [[person|virginia-gregg|Virginia Gregg]] (performer), Hy Averback (performer), and Wally Maher (performer).

Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]], [[org|org.cd82fd99edb39caa|Armed Forces Radio and Television Service]], [[org|org.4798d1172deaae2c|Armed Forces Radio Service]], and [[org|org.17c787dfc8771940|WCBS]].
The stories often return to murder and homicide, robbery and theft, police investigation and procedure, suspect lineups and identification, automobile and traffic crime, and narcotics and drug crime.
